stem:
Tia heats a solid wax crayon gently. At one fixed temperature the solid wax turns into liquid wax.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Heating makes the particles vibrate more until they leave fixed positions; that temperature is the melting point.
Heating packs the particles closer until they stop moving; that temperature is the melting point.
Heating turns the solid straight into vapour; the melting point is the boiling temperature.
The wax melts at any temperature as soon as Tia stirs it.

teacher.key_rationale: Melting is the solid-to-liquid change at the melting point, when particles gain enough vibration to leave fixed positions. Closer packing, calling melting boiling, or melting at any stirred temperature all miss that.
